page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9T34 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, providing 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs via two threads per core. The instance configuration includes 32 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware vector extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache.

The instance operates without bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data, and features a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier single-core compute performance, with stress-ng recording 3114.08, placing it in the top decile of comparable instances. Multi-core execution and overall PassMark metrics align with middle-tier industry averages, scoring 12464.88 in stress-ng multi-core and 14634.27 in PassMark CPU. Memory subsystem testing demonstrates an uncached read bandwidth of 48.51 GB/sec and a write bandwidth of 27.91 GB/sec, while small cached reads reach 616.12 GB/sec. In application benchmarks, the instance delivers 11.25 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.27 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given the balanced core-to-memory ratio, strong single-threaded performance, and absence of local disks or dedicated GPUs, ecs.g8ae.2xlarge is appropriate for enterprise web serving, microservices architectures, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed cache tiers. The inclusion of AVX-512 VNNI and BF16 extensions also supports CPU-based inference and vector calculations without dedicated accelerators. Workloads demanding extreme multi-threaded saturation or local low-latency NVMe scratch storage will experience I/O dependencies on remote block volumes, making this instance best fitted for standard general-purpose compute workloads.
